claims.text: The opt-in ten-feature/head spatial kernel is positive, O(3)-invariant, translation-invariant after graph normalization, permutation-equivariant, and exactly factorized without an edge list or node-pair tensor.
claims.permitted_inference: the implemented feature map, source inspection, dense-reference tests, and full-model symmetry tests
claims.falsifier: a materialized same-kernel reference differs by at least 1e-10, any registered symmetry error reaches 1e-6, or the candidate materializes edge or node-pair state
claims.uncertainty: the finite degree-two feature map is a soft truncated spatial kernel, not an exact Gaussian or hard neighborhood cutoff
claims.next_action: retain the fixed-rank map until a separate accuracy packet compares ranks or learned scales

claims.text: The spatial option is backward-compatible when disabled, adds no learned or persistent state when enabled, and supports the existing coordinate updater with finite gradients.
claims.permitted_inference: matched initialization and train-path tests for the public model
claims.falsifier: the explicit-off output or state differs from default, static spatial changes the persistent state hash, or coordinate/train gradients become nonfinite
claims.uncertainty: checkpoint interoperability was tested through state schema and tensors, not a historical production checkpoint archive
claims.next_action: keep the option false by default

claims.text: On the recorded RTX PRO 6000 FP32 one-graph forward workload at N=8192, static edge-free spatial attention is faster and uses less measured working-plus-edge memory than private static EGNN at k=64 and k=128.
claims.permitted_inference: this hardware, software state, model shapes, synthetic input, forward-only protocol, and confirmed edge multipliers
claims.falsifier: the 100-repeat static/EGNN latency ratio is at least one or memory ratio is at least one at either registered k=64 or k=128 point
claims.uncertainty: the k=64 speed advantage is 2.7% and is hardware, dtype, shape, implementation, and timing-protocol dependent
claims.next_action: treat k=128 as the robust systems win and remeasure k=64 after any environment or kernel change

claims.text: Coordinate-updating edge-free spatial attention is faster than private static EGNN at N=8192,k=64.
claims.permitted_inference: none; this registered prediction was tested and failed
required_evidence: coordinate update included in timed forward
claims.falsifier: not applicable to the retained unsupported claim
claims.uncertainty: dynamic attention was 3.6% slower at k=64 using EGNN latency as the denominator, but faster at exploratory k=80 and registered k=128
claims.next_action: do not promote a dynamic k=64 crossover; optimize coordinate work only if accuracy later justifies it

claims.text: Edge-free spatial attention is universally faster or lower-memory than EGNN across small, sparse, and dense 3D workloads.
